clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year kidney transplant recipient on chronic immunosuppression (prednisone 20 mg/day and mycophenolate 5.760 mg/day) presented with a 1-year history of two painful subcutaneous nodules (2 cm each, firm, barely delimited, adherent, with erythematous and cyanotic overlying skin on the right arm and left forearm) accompanied by constitutional symptoms (fever, cough, weight loss) that began simultaneously with nodule onset. Initial evaluation included negative sputum AFB cultures, which ruled out tuberculosis despite TB-suggestive clinical presentation and pulmonary imaging findings. Biopsy of the right arm nodule revealed histopathologic evidence of macrophage proliferation with rare multinucleated giant cells and lymphoplasma neutrophilic infiltrate. Methenamine silver staining demonstrated abundant intracytoplasmic microorganisms characteristic of Histoplasma capsulatum, sometimes forming hyphae and spores, confirming the diagnosis of disseminated histoplasmosis.
